correctness.rationale: Mahanta–Saikia–Yaqubi Theorem 2.6 gives 2^a p (p≤2^(a+1)−1) Zumkeller, and their Lemma 2.8 preserves Zumkeller under coprime prime-power multiplication; hence v2(z)≥a, vp(z)=1 suffices. For each certified N, CRT combines a square root modulo 2^a with x mod p² such that vp(N−x²)=1, giving 1≤x≤2^a p²≤15376. For N>15376² this yields a positive Zumkeller complement. The p²-good residue count is (p−1)(p+2)/2: nonzero quadratic residues mod p and nonzero multiples of p, disjoint. Binary-square strata have densities 1/2,1/8,1/8,1/4, with independent odd prime CRT failure factors. Independent local enumeration for all ten primes confirmed counts; rational arithmetic recomputed 63520442937841228526/83108492151210387225≈0.7643074888456645. This is only the exact density of the certificate subset and a lower bound on representables, not the true density.
residual_risks: Certificate fraction is not the natural density of all representable N; complement might be much smaller, as conjectured.
Unknown later congruence sieve or larger prime family could duplicate/improve the same 10-prime constant; no exhaustive search.

evidence: Mahanta–Saikia–Yaqubi classifies 2-prime Zumkeller numbers and multiplier closure; Somu–Kukla–Tran posit conjectural density one but no such unconditional stronger coverage result.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Somu–Kukla–Tran (2023) Proposition 4.11 establishes representations on 10 residue classes modulo 18, giving asymptotic coverage at least 5/9; Conjecture 4.21 predicts zero density of exceptions but does not prove it. Mahanta–Saikia–Yaqubi (2020) supplies the two-prime Zumkeller criterion and multiplier facts without additive-square sieve density. The current ten-odd-prime p² sieve and binary stratification produce a strict 0.7643 improvement not implied by the directly examined sources, while relying on their genuine premises.
